title: Retain single-list TypedAxis canonicalization after transient audit

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Audit TypedAxis.__post_init__ for one removable temporary container or repeated traversal while preserving bounded cardinality, exact label validation, duplicate refusal, deterministic lexical canonicalization, direct-constructor error precedence and exact tuple reuse for already canonical axes. Do not add a second axis family, trusted constructor, cache, ordering flag or parameterized cross-contract helper merely to delete bounded validation work.

audit.finding: The current owner already uses the minimum retained container shape for its two input classes. Exact tuple input starts with no list allocation and is returned by identity when labels validate in canonical order. Mutable or non-exact-tuple Sequence input uses exactly one list because the frozen dataclass must take an immutable snapshot. Exact tuple input allocates that same single list only after the first observed inversion, when lexical reordering is actually required.
audit.duplicate_refusal: Adjacent duplicates on an already ordered exact tuple are refused during the first validation pass. Once an inversion requires sorting, duplicate detection must occur after lexical order is established because duplicates may have been non-adjacent in caller order. Replacing the adjacent post-sort scan with a set would add a full hash container, lose the existing no-hash property and provide no bounded-memory improvement.
audit.traversal_analysis: The first pass is required to validate every label before canonical storage. The post-sort adjacent scan occurs only on the fallback path and is required to detect non-adjacent duplicates after canonicalization. Keeping a prefix list from construction start would allocate for the overwhelmingly canonical tuple path; sorting the whole tuple unconditionally would also allocate and add a second full traversal to the canonical path. The current lazy fallback therefore dominates the obvious alternatives under the existing contract.
audit.parallel_abstraction_audit: TensorAxis in daedalus/twin/tensor.py has a similar bounded canonical-label pattern, but it is a different contract owner with a different label-length bound and NUL/refusal surface. Introducing a shared parameterized helper only for these short validation loops would create cross-contract coupling and a new abstraction without removing a semantic owner. GPU-94 therefore does not consolidate the two classes.
audit.gardener_conclusion: Retain the current TypedAxis canonicalization owner unchanged. No production or test edit is justified: the existing relation-axis test owner already pins exact tuple identity reuse, fallback lexical sorting, duplicate refusal and the absence of a full hash-set duplicate detector. Preserve this negative result instead of manufacturing another helper or cache.

coverage: canonical exact tuples are retained by identity
a hash-probe label proves duplicate detection does not materialize a full hash set

result.summary: GPU-94 finds no removable TypedAxis transient that improves the canonical path without adding a container, traversal or abstraction. The existing owner allocates nothing beyond scalars for canonical exact tuples and only one list when snapshotting or reordering is required, so it is retained unchanged.
